docs.text: SpPy ¶ SpPy provides one- and two-dimensional sparse arrays backed by Eigen's C++ sparse matrix library. It stores entries and their coordinates instead of a value for every position, making arrays with many zeros more economical. Use it for sparse vectors and matrices, slicing, arithmetic, reductions, and linear algebra with a NumPy-style interface. import numpy as np import sppy a = sppy.asarray([[0., 2.], [3., 0.]]) product = a @ a # Matrix multiplication squared = a * a # Elementwise multiplication column_sums = a.sum(axis=0) # Dense result: [3., 2.] dense = np.asarray(a) # Explicitly allocate a dense array Start with installation and the quick start , then explore the sparse array guide . Existing users should read the 0.7 migration guide . What to expect ¶ Signed integer storage: int8 , int16 , int32 , and int64 . Floating-point storage: float32 and float64 . Row-major ( order="C" ) and column-major ( order="F" ) matrices. Optional SciPy conversion and Matrix Market IO . Linear solvers, Frobenius norms, and randomized SVD . SpPy requires Python 3.11+, NumPy 2, Eigen 5.0.1+, and a C++17 compiler to build. It supports vectors and matrices, rather than arbitrary-dimensional tensors. Complex, unsigned, and boolean storage are unsupported. NumPy compatibility is partial; see interoperability and limits . Project and support ¶ Report bugs and request features in the GitHub issue tracker . For build problems, include your operating system, Python/compiler versions, Eigen location, command, and full error output. See contributing for validation and documentation commands.

Eigen 5, Cython 3, NumPy 2, and C++17 support. A Pythonic SparseArray interface with compatibility aliases. NumPy-style indexing, matrix multiplication, dtype conversion, and reductions. Optional OpenMP, explicit Eigen discovery, and safer native operations. SciPy Matrix Market IO, formatting checks, and pytest CI. 0.6.7 ¶ 1d arrays can now be pickled Remove string calls for compatibility with Python 3.4 Remove fromScipySparse method (use constructor instead) 0.6.6 ¶ Fix bugs in slicing Turn off bounds checking Element-wise sin, cos, floor, ceil, sign for 2D arrays 0.6.5 ¶ Add methods to support pickling nonzeroRowsPtr method Several bug fixes 0.6.4 ¶ Constructor of csarray accepts scipy.sparse Added io module to read and write matrix market files In csarray: clip, and submatrix methods Various optimisations and bug fixes Better documentation 0.6.3 ¶ Added prune function to remove nnz elements Bug fix for numpy.int32 in csarray. getitem 0.6.2 ¶ Added sppy.linalg.biCGSTAB which solves linear equations of the form Ax = b with x unknown. 0.6.1 ¶ Better documentation Added sppy.linalg.rsvd (randomised Singular Value Decomposition) and sppy.linalg.norm 0.6 ¶ Dot product with numpy arrays, and parallel version (pdot) sppy.linalg.GeneralLinearOperator to work with some scipy.sparse.linalg functions Optimisations to put method Convert from scipy.sparse matrices (csarray.fromScipySparse) Automatic generation of specialised templates during builds (credit: Björn Dahlgren)

Contributing ¶ Set up the development environment before running package checks. Build and preview the documentation ¶ The documentation uses MkDocs and mkdocstrings. API pages are extracted from Python source without importing native extensions, so documentation-only work does not require Eigen, a compiler, or an installed SpPy package. uv sync --locked --only-group docs uv run --locked --only-group docs mkdocs serve Open the local address printed by MkDocs (normally http://127.0.0.1:8000 ). The preview reloads when documentation changes. To build the static site: uv run --locked --only-group docs mkdocs build --strict Output is written to site/ . Strict builds fail on warnings, including broken page links and anchors, and run in CI. Navigation lives in mkdocs.yml ; content lives in docs/*.md . API reference directives read the public Python source. Use relative Markdown links between pages and runnable Python code blocks. --only-group docs installs only documentation dependencies. Run uv sync --locked again before working on native code or running tests. To keep both environments installed, use uv sync --locked --group docs and uv run --locked --group docs mkdocs serve with Eigen configured. Checks and release builds ¶ With the default development environment: uv run --locked pytest uv run --locked ruff check . uv run --locked ruff format --check sppy tests profiling uv run --locked clang-format --dry-run --Werror sppy/include/*.h tests/native/*.cpp profiling/native/*.cpp uv build uv build writes the source distribution and wheel to dist/ . Native binding generation runs in the build directory. setup.py and MANIFEST.in are no longer needed; package and archive settings live in pyproject.toml . After editing dependency declarations, run uv lock and commit the lockfile. After changing external Eigen headers, force a rebuild: uv sync --locked --reinstall-package sppy For optional OpenMP: export SPPY_OPENMP=1 uv sync --locked --reinstall-package sppy uv run --locked pytest uv build The compiler and linker must support OpenMP and its runtime must be available. Keep SPPY_OPENMP set for subsequent commands. Alternatively, release builds accept uv build -Ccmake.define.SPPY_OPENMP=ON . Without OpenMP, parallel kernels run serially. Tests and profiling layout ¶ The pytest suite lives in the repository's top-level tests/ directory. Tests use Arrange–Act–Assert sections, parametrized cases, isolated temporary files, and local random generators. Run a focused subset with, for example, uv run pytest tests/test_numpy_compatibility.py . Native C++ tests are run by pytest when a GCC/Clang compiler and Eigen headers are available; select them with uv run pytest -m native . Missing native prerequisites are reported as skips. sppy.test() locates checkout tests and does not search installed packages. Runtime wheels do not include tests or profiling tools; source archives do. Opt-in profiling tools are in profiling/ . For example: uv run python -m profiling.sparse_array --operation dot --size 1000 uv run python -m profiling.linear_operator --size 1000 --columns 8 uv run python -m profiling.matrix_market --size 1000 uv run python -m profiling.benchmark --operation dot --size 1000 See the profiling guide for workload settings, profile files, and benchmark output. Importing these modules performs no profiling or input generation.

docs.text: Arrays and constructors ¶ For examples and storage behavior, see the sparse array guide . SparseArray is the preferred name; csarray remains a compatibility alias. Constructors ¶ sppy.util ¶ NumPy-style constructors for Eigen sparse arrays. asarray ( a , dtype = None , order = None , * , copy = None ) ¶ Convert to a sparse array, reusing compatible sparse input when possible. Dense input is copied into Eigen storage. Supported dtypes are signed integers (8/16/32/64 bits) and float32/float64. zeros ( shape , dtype = float , storage_type = None , * , order = 'C' , ** kwargs ) ¶ Create an empty sparse array; order selects row or column storage. ones ( shape , dtype = float , storage_type = None , * , order = 'C' , ** kwargs ) ¶ Create an array of ones (every element is stored explicitly). eye ( n , m = None , k = 0 , dtype = float , order = 'C' ) ¶ Create a sparse identity, optionally rectangular or offset by k. The old eye(n, dtype) positional spelling is also accepted. diag ( v , k = 0 , * , order = 'C' , storagetype = None ) ¶ Construct an offset diagonal, or extract one from a matrix. rand ( shape , density , dtype = float , storagetype = 'col' , * , order = None , rng = None ) ¶ Sample sparse values; pass a NumPy Generator for reproducible new code. Coordinates are sampled with replacement, so actual density may be lower than the requested density. The legacy global NumPy RNG remains supported. SparseArray ¶ The constructor accepts a shape or existing data. A tuple is interpreted as a shape; use sppy.asarray to treat a tuple as values. The constructor defaults to column storage; order="C" or order="F" explicitly selects storage. Properties include shape , ndim , size , dtype , order , nnz , and T . nnz counts stored entries; use count_nonzero for nonzero values. parallel_dot aliases pdot ; OpenMP builds can run its kernels in parallel. Without OpenMP, the kernels run serially. sppy . csarray . SparseArray ( S , dtype = None , storagetype = 'col' , * , order = None ) ¶ Create a sparse vector or matrix from a shape or existing data. Parameters: Name Type Description Default S A shape (integer or tuple), dense array, SciPy sparse object, or SparseArray. required dtype A supported NumPy dtype; inferred from data or float64 for a shape. None storagetype One of "row" or "col"; defaults to column storage. 'col' order "C" for row or "F" for column storage; overrides storagetype. None order property ¶ Sparse storage traversal order: 'C' for rows, 'F' for columns. ceil () ¶ Apply numpy.ceil elementwise, including implicit zeros. clip ( min = None , max = None , out = None , ** kwargs ) ¶ Clamp values to bounds as NumPy does, including implicit zeros. compress () ¶ Turn this matrix into compressed sparse format by freeing extra memory space in the buffer. copy ( order = 'K' ) ¶ Return an independent copy, optionally changing sparse storage order. cos () ¶ Apply numpy.cos elementwise, including implicit zeros. diag () ¶ Return a numpy array containing the diagonal entries of this matrix. If the matrix is non-square then the diagonal array is the same size as the smallest dimension. dot ( other ) ¶ Matrix/vector product; equivalent to self @ other . floor () ¶ Apply numpy.floor elementwise, including implicit zeros. getnnz () ¶ Return the number of stored entries, including explicit zeros. multiply ( other ) ¶ Return an elementwise sparse product of equally shaped arrays. max ( axis = None , out = None , keepdims = False ) ¶ Maximum including implicit zeros; empty legacy arrays return NaN. mean ( axis = None , dtype = None , out = None , keepdims = False ) ¶ Compute means without materializing implicit zeros. min ( axis = None , out = None , keepdims = False ) ¶ Minimum including implicit zeros; empty legacy arrays return NaN. nonzero () ¶ Return a tuple of arrays corresponding to nonzero elements. nonzero_rows_list () ¶ Return a list such that the ith element is an array of nonzero elements in the ith row of this matrix. nonzero_rows_ptr () ¶ Returns two arrays indPtr, colInds, such that colInds[indPtr[i]:indPtr[i+1]] is the set of nonzero elements in the ith row of this matrix. pdot ( A ) ¶ Compute the dot product between this and either a csarray or numpy array using multithreading. Parameters: Name Type Description Default A The input numpy array or csarray. required power ( exponent ) ¶ Elementwise power; equivalent to self ** exponent . prune ( eps = 10 ** - 10 , precision = 10 ** - 20 ) ¶ Suppresses all nonzeros which are much smaller in magnitude than eps under the tolerence precision. put ( data , row_indices , colInds , init = False ) ¶ Put some values into this matrix into the corresponding row_indices and colInds. We have A[row_indices[i], colInds[i]] = data[i]/data. Notice that this is faster if init=True but this setting is to be used only if the matrix has just been created. Parameters: Name Type Description Default data Values to assign at the paired row and column indices. required row_indices A 1d numpy array of row indices. required colInds A 1d numpy array of column indices. required reserve ( n ) ¶ Reserve n nonzero entries and turns the matrix into uncompressed mode. Parameters: Name Type Description Default n `int` The number of elements of space to reserve. required row_indices ( i ) ¶ Returns the non zero indices for the ith row. Parameters: Name Type Description Default i `int` The index of the row of the array. required sign () ¶ Apply numpy.sign elementwise, including implicit zeros. sin () ¶ Apply numpy.sin elementwise, including implicit zeros. std ( axis = None , dtype = None , out = None , ddof = 0 , keepdims = False ) ¶ Standard deviation with NumPy-compatible reduction arguments. submatrix ( startRow , startCol , blockRows , blockCols ) ¶ Return a submatrix of the matrix given by A[startRow:startRows+blockRows, startCol:startCol+blockCols] in an efficient manner. Parameters: Name Type Description Default startRow `int` The starting row index required startCol `int` The starting column index required blockRows `int` The number of rows to take. required blockCols `int` The number of columns to take. required sum ( axis = None , dtype = None , out = None , keepdims = False ) ¶ Sum values, including NumPy's axis/dtype/out/keepdims conventions. toarray () ¶ Convert this sparse array into a numpy array. to_scipy_csc () ¶ Convert this matrix to a scipy sparse matrix. Returns a copy of the data in csc_matrix form. to_scipy_csr () ¶ Convert this matrix to a scipy sparse matrix. Returns a copy of the data in csr_matrix form. trace ( offset = 0 , axis1 = 0 , axis2 = 1 , dtype = None , out = None ) ¶ Sum a diagonal, with NumPy's trace arguments. transpose ( * axes ) ¶ Return a copy with axes reversed, following NumPy's transpose convention. values () ¶ Return the values of this object according to the elements returned using nonzero. var ( axis = None , dtype = None , out = None , ddof = 0 , keepdims = False ) ¶ Variance including implicit zeros, using a stable centered sum. astype ( dtype , order = 'K' , casting = 'unsafe' , subok = True , copy = True ) ¶ Cast stored values without allocating a dense array. diagonal ( offset = 0 , axis1 = 0 , axis2 = 1 ) ¶ Extract a diagonal as a dense vector, without densifying the matrix. subarray ( row_indices , column_indices = None ) ¶ Take the Cartesian product of index vectors, like NumPy's ix_. eliminate_zeros () ¶ Remove explicitly stored zeros in place, retaining all nonzero values. column_indices ( column ) ¶ Return stored row indices in a matrix column. count_nonzero ( axis = None ) ¶ Count nonzero values, excluding explicitly stored zeros.

docs.text: Installation ¶ SpPy requires Python 3.11 or newer, Eigen 5.0.1 or newer, and a C++17 compiler. The native build uses scikit-build-core and CMake, with Cython 3.3.1+ and NumPy 2 headers installed automatically in an isolated build environment. CMake and Ninja are provisioned by the backend when suitable tools are not installed. Install uv using https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/. Download and extract Eigen from https://libeigen.gitlab.io/ separately. Creating the development environment ¶ From a source checkout on Linux or macOS: export EIGEN_INCLUDE_DIR=/path/to/eigen-5.0.1 uv sync --locked uv run --locked pytest uv sync creates .venv and installs the project in editable mode, along with the default dev dependency group. No activation is needed for uv run . The committed uv.lock records the resolved dependency versions; .python-version selects Python 3.14. Override the interpreter with, for example, uv sync --locked --python 3.12 . The Eigen include directory must contain Eigen/Core . Installed Eigen CMake packages, standard system include directories, and vendor/eigen are searched when EIGEN_INCLUDE_DIR is unset. On Windows, set the variable in PowerShell: $env:EIGEN_INCLUDE_DIR = "C:\path\to\eigen-5.0.1" uv sync --locked uv run --locked pytest Use an MSVC developer shell with C++17 support. Linux is validated locally; macOS and Windows have not been validated locally. Minimal environments and SciPy ¶ To omit development dependencies: uv sync --locked --no-dev uv run --locked --no-dev python -c "import sppy; print(sppy.__version__)" For SciPy interoperability and Matrix Market IO, add --extra scipy to sync and run commands. The default development group already includes SciPy. Install with pip ¶ uv is a development convenience, not a runtime dependency. From a source checkout with Eigen configured, a regular installation is supported: python -m pip install . python -m pip install '.[scipy]' The second command also installs SciPy. Source installations need the same compiler and Eigen headers as development builds. Troubleshooting ¶ Eigen not found: point EIGEN_INCLUDE_DIR at the directory containing Eigen/Core , rather than the Eigen subdirectory itself. Use Eigen 5.0.1+. Compiler errors: check that a C++17 compiler is available. On Windows, use an MSVC developer shell. SciPy import errors: add --extra scipy to both uv sync and uv run when using --no-dev . Stale native build: run uv sync --locked --reinstall-package sppy after updating external Eigen headers. For checks, OpenMP builds, release artifacts, and documentation previews, see contributing .

docs.text: NumPy and SciPy interoperability ¶ NumPy ¶ SpPy follows common NumPy naming and indexing conventions, but does not implement the complete array-function or ufunc dispatch protocols. Prefer methods such as a.sum(axis=0) and operators such as a @ b to keep the conversion boundary explicit. import numpy as np import sppy a = sppy.asarray([[0, 2], [3, 0]], dtype=np.int64) dense = np.asarray(a) assert dense.dtype == np.int64 assert a.sum() == 5 Dense conversion preserves the stored dtype, including exact int64 values. np.asarray(a) always allocates dense storage. Other NumPy functions may also coerce to dense arrays; do not assume they preserve sparsity. Supported storage dtypes are signed 8/16/32/64-bit integers and 32/64-bit floats. Boolean, unsigned, and complex storage are unsupported. Arrays have one or two dimensions. Individual dimensions and stored-entry indices use signed 32-bit limits. General arithmetic broadcasting, whole-array boolean masks, new-axis indexing, and the full set of NumPy reduction keywords are unsupported. SciPy sparse arrays and matrices ¶ Install the scipy extra as described in installation . The default development environment already includes SciPy. from scipy import sparse import sppy source = sparse.csr_array([[0., 2.], [3., 0.]]) a = sppy.asarray(source) csr = a.to_scipy_csr() csc = a.to_scipy_csc() Use the constructor or asarray for conversion into SpPy. There is no fromScipySparse method. Conversion allocates new storage. Matrix Market files ¶ from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory from pathlib import Path import sppy from sppy.io import mmread, mmwrite with TemporaryDirectory() as directory: path = Path(directory) / "matrix.mtx" mmwrite(path, sppy.eye(3), comment="Example identity matrix") restored = mmread(path) assert restored.shape == (3, 3) Matrix Market IO requires two-dimensional arrays and SciPy. The reader supports comments, symmetry, and compressed input through SciPy. Integer files are loaded as int64 , real files as float64 ; complex values are rejected. See the IO reference for arguments and storage selection.

docs.text: Linear algebra ¶ Import functions from sppy.linalg . The solver uses floating-point sparse matrices; randomized SVD also accepts dense arrays and general linear operators. Solve a linear system ¶ import numpy as np import sppy from sppy.linalg import bicgstab, norm a = sppy.asarray([[4., 1.], [1., 3.]]) b = np.array([1., 2.]) x, status = bicgstab(a, b, rtol=1e-10) assert status == 0 np.testing.assert_allclose(a @ x, b) frobenius = norm(a) Always inspect status : 0 means success, 1 a numerical issue, 2 no convergence, and 3 invalid input. These are SpPy's codes and differ from SciPy's convention. norm computes only the Frobenius norm; its ord argument is currently ignored. Randomized SVD ¶ from sppy.linalg import rsvd u, singular_values, v = rsvd(a, k=1, p=1, q=2) approximation = (u * singular_values) @ v.T assert approximation.shape == a.shape rsvd returns right singular vectors as columns of v , rather than returning v.T . Increase p (oversampling) or q (power iterations) to improve the approximation. Sampling uses NumPy's global random state. Functions ¶ sppy.linalg.core ¶ bicgstab ( a , b , * , maxiter = 1000 , rtol = 1e-06 ) ¶ Solve a floating-point sparse linear system; return (solution, status). Status codes retain SpPy's convention: 0 success, 1 numerical issue, 2 no convergence, 3 invalid input. norm ( A , ord = None ) ¶ This function returns the Frobenius norm of the input A, which is defined as sqrt(sum A_ij^2). Parameters: Name Type Description Default A A csarray object. required ord The type of norm required, currently ignored. None Returns: Type Description The Frobenius norm of A. rsvd ( A , k , p = 10 , q = 2 , omega = None ) ¶ Compute the randomised SVD using the algorithm on page 9 of Halko et al., Finding Structure with randomness: stochastic algorithms for constructing approximate matrix decompositions, 2009. Finds the partial SVD of a sparse or dense matrix A, resolving the largest k singular vectors/values, using exponent q and k+p projections. Returns the left and right singular vectors, and the singular values. The resulting matrix can be approximated using A ~ U s V.T. To improve the approximation quality for a fixed k, increase p or q. Parameters: Name Type Description Default A A sparse or dense matrix or GeneralLinearOperator required k The number of singular values and random projections required p The oversampling parameter 10 q The exponent for the projections. 2 omega An initial matrix to perform random projections onto with at least k columns None Returns: Type Description The right singular vectors biCGSTAB ( A , b , maxIter = 1000 , tol = 10 ** - 6 ) ¶ Solve the linear system of equations given by A x = b where A is a csarray and b is a numpy array of the same dtype. Uses the Iterative stabilized bi-conjugate gradient method. Parameters: Name Type Description Default A A csarray object of size n x n required b A numpy array of length n of the same dtype as A. required maxIter The maximum number of iteartions of the method 1000 tol The error tolerance 10 ** -6 Returns: Type Description The output code: 0 = success, 1 = numerical Issue, 2 = no convergence, 3 = invalid input General linear operators ¶ Wrap a matrix with GeneralLinearOperator.as_linear_operator(a) to expose matvec , rmatvec , matmat , and rmatmat callbacks. Combine operators lazily with as_linear_operator_sum(left, right) . sppy.linalg.general_linear_operator.GeneralLinearOperator ¶ Bases: object A more general form of LinearOperator in scipy.linalg. Can be used with many of the scipy functions. The new operation is rmatmat which is X.T V. __init__ ( shape , matvec , rmatvec = None , matmat = None , rmatmat = None , add = None , dtype = None ) ¶ as_linear_operator ( X , parallel = False ) staticmethod ¶ Make a general linear operator from csarray X. as_linear_operator_sum ( X , Y ) staticmethod ¶ Take two linear operators X and Y, and operate on their sum, using lazy evaluation.

docs.text: Migrating to 0.7 ¶ The Python interface is ordinary, formatted Python; typed Cython 3 extensions implement the Eigen kernels. SpPy supports one- and two-dimensional arrays with signed integer (8/16/32/64 bit) or float32/float64 values. Complex, unsigned, and boolean storage are not yet supported. NumPy-style usage ¶ import numpy as np import sppy a = sppy.asarray([[0., 2.], [3., 0.]], order="C") b = sppy.eye(2, dtype=np.float64) product = a @ b # SparseArray elementwise = a * b # SparseArray vector = a @ np.ones(2) # ndarray row = a[0] # one-dimensional SparseArray reversed_rows = a[::-1] means = np.mean(a, axis=0, keepdims=True) single = a.astype(np.float32) dense = np.asarray(a) # explicitly allocates dense storage scipy_csr = a.to_scipy_csr() asarray infers the input dtype. Compatible sparse input can be reused with copy=False ; conversion from dense input always needs a copy. zeros , ones , and eye default to C (row) order, as NumPy does. The legacy SparseArray(shape) / csarray(shape) constructor retains column order unless order is supplied. A tuple passed to the constructor specifies a shape; use asarray to interpret a tuple as data. Renamed APIs ¶ Preferred Compatibility alias SparseArray csarray to_scipy_csr toScipyCsr to_scipy_csc toScipyCsc row_indices rowInds column_indices colInds subarray subArray nonzero_rows_list nonzeroRowsList nonzero_rows_ptr nonzeroRowsPtr parallel_dot pdot multiply hadamard diagonal diag (main diagonal) linalg.bicgstab linalg.biCGSTAB as_linear_operator asLinearOperator as_linear_operator_sum asLinearOperatorSum The linear operator implementation lives in sppy.linalg.general_linear_operator ; the old module remains importable. bicgstab accepts maxiter and rtol ; its legacy wrapper retains maxIter and tol . Solver status codes retain SpPy's convention, documented in the function, rather than SciPy's codes. Intentional behavior changes ¶ Integer indexing drops an axis. Negative assignments, reversed/stepped slices, per-axis boolean masks, and broadcasting of paired indices work like NumPy. Sparse slices are independent copies, including basic slices. * is elementwise and @ is matrix multiplication. Sparse addition, subtraction, and elementwise multiplication require matching shapes; general arithmetic broadcasting is not implemented. Nonzero scalar addition raises NotImplementedError because it would fill implicit zeros. Reductions accept axis , out , and keepdims . Sum, mean, variance, and standard deviation also support dtype ; variance and standard deviation accept ddof . Reduction results are dense scalars or arrays. Empty min/max retain the historical NaN result. Dense conversion preserves dtype, including exact int64 values. Arithmetic promotes dtypes, and sum promotes small integers as NumPy does. clip clamps values rather than discarding out-of-range entries. ceil and floor follow NumPy's output dtype rather than always int64. cos includes implicit zeros, so its result can store every element. eliminate_zeros removes only exact stored zeros. prune remains the tolerance-based operation. nnz counts stored entries; count_nonzero excludes stored zeros. SciPy is optional for conversion and Matrix Market IO. The maintained SciPy reader handles coordinate formats, comments, symmetry, and compressed files. Limits ¶ There is no complete implementation of NumPy's array-function/ufunc dispatch. np.asarray explicitly densifies; NumPy operations that coerce their arguments may also densify. Prefer sparse methods and operators for large arrays. New-axis indexing, whole-array boolean masks, more than two dimensions, and the full set of NumPy reduction keyword arguments are not supported. Stored-entry indices and individual dimensions use signed 32-bit limits. OpenMP is optional and its absence makes parallel kernels serial. CI covers Linux; macOS and Windows have not been validated locally.

docs.text: Quick start ¶ After installing SpPy , run these examples in Python. Create an array ¶ Use asarray to convert data and zeros to create an empty sparse array. The conversion infers the dtype; pass dtype explicitly when needed. import numpy as np import sppy a = sppy.asarray([[0., 2., 0.], [3., 0., 4.]]) assert a.shape == (2, 3) assert a.ndim == 2 assert a.size == 6 assert a.nnz == 3 b = sppy.zeros((2, 3), dtype=np.float64) b[0, 1] = 2. b[1, [0, 2]] = [3., 4.] np.testing.assert_array_equal(a.toarray(), b.toarray()) size counts all positions, while nnz counts stored entries. Explicitly stored zeros can contribute to nnz ; use count_nonzero() to count nonzero values. Select and update values ¶ row = a[0] # Sparse vector with shape (3,) column = a[:, 1] # Sparse vector with shape (2,) block = a[:, 1:] # Sparse matrix with shape (2, 2) a[-1, 0] = 5. assert a[1, 0] == 5. Slices are independent copies. Assign through a[...] to change the original. Compute with sparse arrays ¶ squared = a * a product = a @ a.T vector_product = a @ np.ones(3) row_totals = a.sum(axis=1) means = a.mean(axis=0, keepdims=True) assert product.shape == (2, 2) np.testing.assert_array_equal(vector_product, [2., 9.]) np.testing.assert_array_equal(row_totals, [2., 9.]) * multiplies elementwise; @ performs matrix multiplication. Reductions and products with dense vectors return dense results. For larger workloads, read the sparse array guide before converting to dense arrays.

docs.text: Sparse arrays ¶ Construction, dtypes, and storage ¶ import numpy as np import sppy empty = sppy.zeros((5, 7), dtype=np.float32) vector = sppy.zeros(5, dtype=np.int64) identity = sppy.eye(5) diagonal = sppy.diag(np.array([1., 2., 3.])) random = sppy.rand((5, 7), 0.1, rng=np.random.default_rng(21)) columns = sppy.asarray([[0., 2.], [3., 0.]], order="F") Use asarray for data, including tuples. In SparseArray((5, 7)) , the tuple specifies a shape instead of values. asarray infers the input dtype. zeros , ones , and eye default to row storage ( order="C" ). The direct SparseArray constructor and rand retain the legacy column-storage default. Choose order="F" for column storage and order="C" for row storage. rand samples coordinates with replacement, so the resulting density may be lower than requested. Pass a NumPy Generator for reproducible inputs. Integer dtypes cast the random values, which can produce stored zeros. ones stores every element explicitly. asarray(a) may reuse a compatible sparse array. Request copy=True for an independent object; copy=False raises if conversion requires allocation. Dense inputs always require a copy into Eigen storage. a.copy() and a.astype(np.float32) provide explicit copying and dtype conversion. Indexing and assignment ¶ Integer indices drop an axis; slices preserve it. Negative indices, reversed or stepped slices, per-axis boolean masks, and paired array indices are supported. A slice is a copy, including a basic slice. a = sppy.asarray([[0., 2., 0.], [3., 0., 4.]]) row = a[0] # Shape (3,) rows = a[:1] # Shape (1, 3) reversed_rows = a[::-1] masked = a[np.array([True, False]), :] paired = a[[0, 1], [1, 2]] # Select (0, 1) and (1, 2) cartesian = a.subarray([0, 1], [1, 2]) # Select a 2 by 2 submatrix a[[0, 1], [0, 1]] = [5., 6.] a[:, 2] = 1. Paired indices select coordinate pairs; subarray selects the Cartesian product of row and column indices. Whole-array boolean masks and None (new-axis) indexing are unsupported. Assemble a matrix ¶ Reserve space when the approximate entry count is known, insert entries, then compress to release spare buffer capacity. a = sppy.zeros((1000, 1000)) a.reserve(3) a[[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]] = [0.1, 0.2, 0.4] a.compress() Arithmetic and reductions ¶ Expression Operation Result a + b , a - b Same-shape sparse arithmetic Sparse array a * b , a.multiply(b) Same-shape elementwise product Sparse array a * 2 , -a , abs(a) Scalar multiplication, negation, absolute value Sparse array a @ b , a.dot(b) Matrix product of sparse matrices Sparse array a @ dense_vector Matrix-vector product Dense array a.T Transpose Sparse array a.sum(axis=0) Column sums Dense array a.diagonal() Main diagonal Dense array A sparse vector dotted with another sparse vector returns a scalar. Sparse arithmetic promotes dtypes. General arithmetic broadcasting is unsupported, and nonzero scalar addition raises NotImplementedError . sum , mean , min , max , var , and std accept axis , out , and keepdims . Sum, mean, variance, and standard deviation also accept dtype ; variance and standard deviation accept ddof . Implicit zeros participate in reductions. Empty min/max retain the historical NaN result. Stored zeros and memory ¶ a.nnz counts stored entries, including stored zeros. a.count_nonzero() counts nonzero values. a.eliminate_zeros() removes exact zeros in place; a.prune() removes entries using a tolerance. Operations that can fill an array a.toarray() and np.asarray(a) allocate dense storage. ones , cos , clipping to a positive lower bound, and other operations that map zero to a nonzero value can store every position. Estimate the full array size before applying these operations to large shapes. Prefer sparse methods when memory matters. NumPy interoperability explains the conversion boundaries, and the API reference lists the available methods.
docs.title: Sparse arrays

docs.text: import numpy as np import sppy empty = sppy.zeros((5, 7), dtype=np.float32) vector = sppy.zeros(5, dtype=np.int64) identity = sppy.eye(5) diagonal = sppy.diag(np.array([1., 2., 3.])) random = sppy.rand((5, 7), 0.1, rng=np.random.default_rng(21)) columns = sppy.asarray([[0., 2.], [3., 0.]], order="F") Use asarray for data, including tuples. In SparseArray((5, 7)) , the tuple specifies a shape instead of values. asarray infers the input dtype. zeros , ones , and eye default to row storage ( order="C" ). The direct SparseArray constructor and rand retain the legacy column-storage default. Choose order="F" for column storage and order="C" for row storage. rand samples coordinates with replacement, so the resulting density may be lower than requested. Pass a NumPy Generator for reproducible inputs. Integer dtypes cast the random values, which can produce stored zeros. ones stores every element explicitly. asarray(a) may reuse a compatible sparse array. Request copy=True for an independent object; copy=False raises if conversion requires allocation. Dense inputs always require a copy into Eigen storage. a.copy() and a.astype(np.float32) provide explicit copying and dtype conversion.
docs.title: Construction, dtypes, and storage

docs.text: Integer indices drop an axis; slices preserve it. Negative indices, reversed or stepped slices, per-axis boolean masks, and paired array indices are supported. A slice is a copy, including a basic slice. a = sppy.asarray([[0., 2., 0.], [3., 0., 4.]]) row = a[0] # Shape (3,) rows = a[:1] # Shape (1, 3) reversed_rows = a[::-1] masked = a[np.array([True, False]), :] paired = a[[0, 1], [1, 2]] # Select (0, 1) and (1, 2) cartesian = a.subarray([0, 1], [1, 2]) # Select a 2 by 2 submatrix a[[0, 1], [0, 1]] = [5., 6.] a[:, 2] = 1. Paired indices select coordinate pairs; subarray selects the Cartesian product of row and column indices. Whole-array boolean masks and None (new-axis) indexing are unsupported.

docs.text: Reserve space when the approximate entry count is known, insert entries, then compress to release spare buffer capacity. a = sppy.zeros((1000, 1000)) a.reserve(3) a[[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]] = [0.1, 0.2, 0.4] a.compress()

docs.text: Expression Operation Result a + b , a - b Same-shape sparse arithmetic Sparse array a * b , a.multiply(b) Same-shape elementwise product Sparse array a * 2 , -a , abs(a) Scalar multiplication, negation, absolute value Sparse array a @ b , a.dot(b) Matrix product of sparse matrices Sparse array a @ dense_vector Matrix-vector product Dense array a.T Transpose Sparse array a.sum(axis=0) Column sums Dense array a.diagonal() Main diagonal Dense array A sparse vector dotted with another sparse vector returns a scalar. Sparse arithmetic promotes dtypes. General arithmetic broadcasting is unsupported, and nonzero scalar addition raises NotImplementedError . sum , mean , min , max , var , and std accept axis , out , and keepdims . Sum, mean, variance, and standard deviation also accept dtype ; variance and standard deviation accept ddof . Implicit zeros participate in reductions. Empty min/max retain the historical NaN result.
docs.title: Arithmetic and reductions

docs.text: a.nnz counts stored entries, including stored zeros. a.count_nonzero() counts nonzero values. a.eliminate_zeros() removes exact zeros in place; a.prune() removes entries using a tolerance. Operations that can fill an array a.toarray() and np.asarray(a) allocate dense storage. ones , cos , clipping to a positive lower bound, and other operations that map zero to a nonzero value can store every position. Estimate the full array size before applying these operations to large shapes. Prefer sparse methods when memory matters.
